items.definition: A choice you make after thinking about different possibilities. In English you make a decision; you do not take or do one in the same way.
examples: It was a difficult decision, but I think we made the right one.
The committee will announce its decision on Monday.

items.definition: Careful study of a subject to discover new facts. It is uncountable, so it has no plural and no a/an.
examples: She is doing research into sleep and memory.
The research suggests that short breaks improve concentration.

items.definition: The vehicles moving along a road. We describe the amount with heavy or light, not strong or big.
examples: We were late because of the heavy traffic on the ring road.
The traffic is usually light on Sunday mornings.

items.definition: The possibility that something bad will happen. Verbs that go with it are take, run and pose.
examples: Investors who take big risks can lose all their money.
Smoking poses a serious risk to your health.

items.definition: Careful interest in someone or something. You pay attention, not do or put attention.
examples: Please pay attention to the instructions on the screen.
The advert caught my attention straight away.

items.definition: Physical or mental energy that you use to do something difficult.
examples: He made a real effort to arrive on time all week.
It took a lot of effort to learn the vocabulary for the exam.

items.definition: Something you do or think that is wrong. You make a mistake; you do not do one.
examples: I made a silly mistake when I filled in the form.
It would be a big mistake to ignore the warning.

items.definition: Development towards a better or more advanced state. It is uncountable: you make progress, never makes progresses.
examples: The students have made steady progress this term.
There has been very little progress in the talks.

items.definition: An arranged time to see someone, especially a doctor, dentist or other professional.
examples: I've made an appointment to see the dentist on Thursday.
Sorry, I have to cancel my appointment because of a meeting.

items.definition: Money that a business earns after paying all its costs.
examples: The bakery made a small profit in its first year.
The company reported a sharp fall in profits.
